chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Una Mae Carlisle's decline on the bandstand
summary: Pretty but limited, Una Mae turned strange between sets and could not play or sing by showtime; he declines to say what he thinks caused it.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: I don't know, Fats must have been in Europe then, or something, because he -- at that time he was in and out, and when he come in town he would grab a couple
of guys, go to Boston, around through New England and play a few things, which I didn't do with him.
Yeah, I wasn't interested, and of course he only I mean Una did two -- a couple of nights here, a couple of days there, one of those things. You know.
But this was before you went with Stuff, though.
This was after you had been with Stuff? Oh. So that -- is that how you got Una Mae Carlisle?

Well, Una Mae, Una Mae came back from Europe, and she did a few things with us in the Apollo Theater, and Fats was trying to help them push her, you know. And she didn't go so well, and she was just pretty, most beautiful thing in the world, for years, but abilities, I mean didn't really stand up. It didn't go too well. It wasn't too good. And after that she started recording, and finally went on her own [-- well, on, and after she was here a while she began to act up, things, I think went kind of badly for her, because I didn't know it at the time, but when we got ready to go on she'd be sitting with a party, and looking -- I mean she was beautiful. Looked like any normal person, to me. And they'd

hit the gong, and they would announce, Ladies and Gentlemen, in a few minutes we will now bring you the show. The show will go on such and so and so and so and so, and about 15 minutes the show who on, and I'd call her out, and she'd come out looking like Dracula, or somebody.

Just that quick. You know, (Unintelligible) remember, and -- I didn't know what the heck to do. I mean I didn't -- I didn't know she was like that. I mean I'd never seen her that way. And she'd sit at the piano and she couldn't play, she couldn't sing, she couldn't talk. So I mean, what the heck? You know?
I still don't know. I couldn't swear, but well, I had my own -- like everybody's notions, I guess, but what the hell. I can't -- still can't prove it, or nothing, and I still won't say.
Because what I think could -- I could be wrong. But I mean that quick, in 15 minutes, 20 minutes, what the hell.
We could just sort of figure.
